cells.tense: Right now the first clear look is here with you, and it has not cut anything yet.
cells.act: go all the way into the pattern until you meet its edge
cells.ask: Follow whatever pulls at you next into how it actually fits together, all the way to the edge of what you can make out — then stop, without deciding. What lies past that edge can stay as it is.
cells.core:
A new clarity is here in you at its first cut. Take something that pulls you toward what you genuinely want and follow it in — not to a conclusion, only into how it fits together — and stop at the edge of what you can make out. The pull keeps pointing; the following is yours, and it does not have to land anywhere yet.

There's a depth in you that finds the pattern and stops before it flatters itself. It lives in the thing that draws you, not in proving you've understood it. Let that one stay undecided a while longer. What you'll have is an honest look at the shape of it, and the ground under your pull sits a little steadier. Less gets tangled on the way out.
cells.sheetLine: You can look clearly at what draws you, and stop at the edge.
cells.verb: seeing clearly before the shape of what is seen is settled
cells.place: where the pull toward what is genuinely wanted is felt

cells.tense: It will still be unfolding, and you will already be deciding what it will be by then.
cells.act: bring the possibility all the way into form
cells.ask: Carry one half-formed thing you're drawn to into form at the size it actually is — small, unfinished — and let it sit that way this week instead of finished in your head.
cells.core:
Where the pull toward what you want is felt in you, perceiving runs past the thing perceived. How it will end up is already worked out, so each stage it is actually in reads as a stage rather than a thing. What's clear to you gets carried beyond what's here, and the version sitting in this moment doesn't get its own look from anyone, including you.

Let one thing you're drawn to stand as it is right now, before perceiving completes it. Bring it into form at exactly the size it is, small and unfinished, and let that be all of it for seven days. It will feel like missing the point. It isn't: the next clear look arrives when there is something here to look at, and the pull gets to be about what's actually present instead of what you can predict. The real thing finally meets your eyes.
cells.sheetLine: You see what it will be before it's been what it is.
cells.verb: seeing clearly before the shape of what is seen is settled
cells.place: where the pull toward what is genuinely wanted is felt

cells.tense: The clear look landed a while back, and you have stayed where it found you.
cells.act: bring the directed work to its full standing
cells.ask: Take what you've already seen clearly and do the next small piece of it that finishing would need. Real and specific, no plan. Just the piece, done.
cells.core:
The clear look is in you. It landed, and the place where the pull toward what you want is felt hasn't moved since — what's clear to you is described, decided, known, and nothing has been built on top of it. Perceiving happens in the past tense around here now: you remember what you saw, you can say what's true, and the direction has stopped pointing anywhere in particular.

Do one small piece of the thing you've already seen clearly, the piece that building it would actually require. Real and specific, no plan attached. It doesn't have to start anything. It's the next piece, done, and it will hold whether or not you feel like it did. True sight returns through your hands before it returns through your eyes sometimes, and what you'll have is something solid where there was only a clear look.
cells.sheetLine: You saw what's true. You've stayed where it found you.
cells.verb: seeing clearly before the shape of what is seen is settled
cells.place: where the pull toward what is genuinely wanted is felt

cells.tense: Perceiving is happening through you right now, and you're filing it as simply what's obvious.
cells.act: notice what is newly here, right now
cells.ask: Catch the moment today when something new landed about what sits around you — mark it to yourself, in your own words. Then find a detail you can see now that wasn't there yesterday.
cells.core:
There's a clear look happening here, and if anyone asked where it came from you'd point at the situation — it's just what's plain, anyone would see it. Meanwhile the pull toward what you actually want keeps orienting on something you haven't noticed you chose, and perceiving that finds it keeps getting filed under circumstance. What you're seeing is real. Who is doing the perceiving has been left off the page.

Catch a thing you can see right now that wasn't there yesterday, and mark the moment you first caught it. No bigger than that. What you'll get is how much of the orientation is yours; perceiving stays exactly as clear, and it has an author at the table again. The next thing that arrives gets met while it's still arriving, not after it has turned into the obvious.
cells.sheetLine: The clear look is yours, filed under what's obvious.
cells.verb: seeing clearly before the shape of what is seen is settled
cells.place: where the pull toward what is genuinely wanted is felt

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person's own direction and pull are authored by them and simply unrecognized — a Bound at Fruition with a disowned present may have had that authorship taken rather than mislaid, and the cell narrows to what the capacity is doing now, not what happened. A reader could reasonably say the seeing is not clear at all, just unnamed; the ask survives that because noticing what is newly here works whether or not the read is right. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line suggesting their aim arrives whole once the seeing is counted — I cut that and left it as a count, not a result.
